newsitem.title: USA: U.S. journalists' group adopts new code of ethics.
newsitem.headline: U.S. journalists' group adopts new code of ethics.

text.p: Spurred into action by public debate about media fairness and objectivity, the biggest U.S. journalism organisation Saturday approved a new, revised code of ethics committed to "public enlightenment."
The Society of Professional Journalists, wrapping up its four-day annual conference, voted to approve the new code of ethics, developed over the past two years.

The document begins with a preamble recognising that "public enlightenment is the forerunner of justice and the foundation of democracy." It says the journalist's duty is to further those ends by seeking the truth and providing a "fair and comprehensive account of events and issues."

The code of ethics urges journalists to seek truth and report it; minimise harm to sources, subjects and colleagues; act independently; and be accountable to their readers, listeners, viewers, as well as each other.

"We think two years of debate over this code has been worth it," said Kevin Smith, of Miami University in Ohio, who headed the revision effort. "I believe we have a solid code that speaks to many of the ethical issues today's journalists face."

The code includes many specific recommendations spelling out ethical behaviour on everything from identification of sources and acceptable image enhancement of news photographs, to guidelines on how to avoid conflicts of interest.
The guidelines also address the need to avoid stereotyping and "tell the story of the diversity and magnitude of the human experience boldly, even when it is unpopular to do so."
They urge journalists to remain free of associations and activities that may compromise their integrity or damage their credibility, as well as refusing gifts, favours, fees, and free travel.
